To calculate the molecular weight of the newly discovered compound based on the observed
freezing point depression of water, we first apply the freezing point depression formula:
ΔTf = Kf \times m, where ΔTf is the change in freezing point, Kf is the freezing point
depression constant for water (1.86 ^\circC kg/mol), and m is the molality of the
solution. The observed depression of -1.22^\circC indicates that ΔTf = 1.22^\circC.
Rearranging the equation to find molality gives m = ΔTf/Kf = 1.22 ^\circC / 1.86 ^\circC
kg/mol = 0.656 mol/kg. Since the mass of the solute is 2.00 grams, we convert this to
kilograms (0.002 kg), and using the definition of molality (m = moles of solute/kg of
solvent), we determine the number of moles of the compound: moles = 0.656 mol/kg \times
0.002 kg = 0.001312 mol. Finally, the molecular weight (MW) can be calculated using the
formula MW = mass of solute / moles of solute = 2.00 g / 0.001312 mol, resulting in a
molecular weight of approximately 305 g/mole.
